description: Contact energy between adjacent Endothelial Cells (EC). Lower values promote stronger adhesion and cell-cell cohesion. This is the J parameter in the Cellular Potts Model Hamiltonian.
admissible_note: J must be ≥ 0: a negative contact energy rewards boundary creation and cells fragment despite the connectivity constraint. At the upper end J ≫ T (T = 5) makes boundary moves essentially never accepted (Boltzmann factor e^(−ΔE/T)); 100 = 20 T is the modeler's cap, not a measured limit.
supported_evidence: expert_judgement: Merks RMH et al. (2006), Merks RMH et al. (2008); Merks et al. 2006, Fig 7 (J_cc = 20…1 at J_cM = 20, T = 50), p. 49
supported_note: The papers give no measured J; their values live on a T = 50 scale (J_cc 1–40). Rescaled to this model's T = 5 that is J_EE ≈ 0.1–4. The 2–16 band is the model author's exploration range in the model's own units: 2 keeps cells adhesive (γ = 1), 16 is strongly repulsive (γ = −6) and the network fragments. Labelled expert judgement because the published ranges do not transfer across the 10× temperature difference.
recommended_note: The preset set (strong 2 / moderate 4 / weak 8) spans the band; above 8 γ turns negative with J_EM = 2 and EC–EC contact is disfavoured. Not calibrated against data.
default_locator: angiogenesis_process.py, _run_simulation() specs: ContactPlugin.param_new("EC", "EC", jee); PottsCore fluctuation_amplitude=5.0

description: Contact energy between Endothelial Cells and the surrounding medium. Higher values cause cells to minimize medium contact, promoting aggregation into compact clusters.
admissible_note: J ≥ 0 required (negative J rewards cell–medium boundary and cells dissolve into the medium). 100 = 20 T is the modeler's cap, where medium-contact moves are never accepted.
supported_evidence: expert_judgement: Merks RMH et al. (2008), Merks RMH et al. (2006); Merks et al. 2008, Methods (Cellular Potts model; chemotaxis; chemoattractant dynamics)
supported_note: Merks et al. hold J(c,M) fixed at 20 (T = 50) in every published run, i.e. the single point J/T = 0.4 = this model's default. The 2–16 band is the model author's exploration range: with J_EE = 2 it moves γ from 1 (network) to 15 (compact islands).
recommended_note: Preset set (network 2 / moderate 4 / strong 8 / extreme 12). The GUI's own "aggregation study" preset uses 8. Not calibrated against data.

description: Coefficient determining the strength of directed cell migration up VEGF gradients. Higher values mean stronger chemotactic response.
admissible_evidence: literature: Merks RMH et al. (2008); Merks et al. 2008, Methods: "χ(c,M) = 500 (standard; varied to 0–5,000)"
admissible_note: Exactly the range Merks et al. 2008 swept (0–5,000). λ = 0 switches chemotaxis off; above ≈5,000 at T = 5 the chemotaxis term dominates every copy attempt and cells stream up the gradient regardless of adhesion or volume.
supported_evidence: expert_judgement: Merks RMH et al. (2008); Merks et al. 2008, Methods (Cellular Potts model; chemotaxis; chemoattractant dynamics)
supported_note: 0–1,000 brackets the two published standards (500 in 2008, 1,000 in 2006) and the preset set. Not a measured quantity: λ is a CPM coupling, calibrated by the authors against the velocity of 5 µm/h (up to 30 µm/h) they report for endothelial cells.
recommended_note: Presets weak 200 / moderate 500 / strong 800. 100–800 is the window in which the default parameter set still forms a connected network at T = 5; not calibrated.

description: Saturation parameter for chemotaxis response. Controls whether chemotaxis is linear (0) or saturating (>0) with concentration.
admissible_note: s ≥ 0 required (a negative s makes the denominator vanish at c = −1/s). At s = 1 the response is already half-saturated at c = 1, the steady-state concentration inside cells for α = ε; above that chemotaxis is effectively flat.
supported_evidence: literature: Merks RMH et al. (2008); Merks et al. 2008, Methods (Cellular Potts model; chemotaxis; chemoattractant dynamics)
supported_note: Merks et al. 2008 explore s from 0 to 0.15. The band 0–0.1 is that sweep clipped at the model default; 0.15 would be the literature-backed ceiling.
recommended_evidence: literature: Merks RMH et al. (2008); Merks et al. 2008, Methods (Cellular Potts model; chemotaxis; chemoattractant dynamics)
recommended_note: Same as the physiological band: linear (0) or saturating (0.1), both inside the published sweep.
literature: Merks RMH, Perryn ED, Shirinifard A, Glazier JA. Contact-inhibited chemotaxis in de novo and sprouting blood-vessel growth. PLoS Comput Biol. 2008;4(9):e1000163.

description: Rate at which VEGF is degraded or cleared from the medium. Higher values shorten VEGF range.
admissible_note: ε ≥ 0 required. The explicit decay update c ← c(1 − εΔt) changes sign for ε > 1 per MCS; DiffusionSolverFE's sub-stepping keeps εΔt_sub < 1, so 2 is the modeler's cap rather than the hard limit.
supported_evidence: expert_judgement: Merks RMH et al. (2008), Merks RMH et al. (2006); Merks et al. 2008, Methods (ε = α = 1e-3 s⁻¹); Merks et al. 2006, Results (1.8e-4 s⁻¹), p. 50
supported_note: 0.1–0.5 per MCS is the model author's band around the default. On the Merks scale the literature values are 0.0054–0.03 per MCS and VEGF165's 30–60 min half-life gives 0.006–0.012 per MCS, all BELOW this band. Labelled expert judgement, not literature, for that reason; see the default-value note for the consequence (shorter gradients).
recommended_note: Presets 0.1 / 0.3 / 0.5. Keep veder and vesec equal if the Merks α = ε steady state (c = 1 inside cells) is to be preserved, otherwise the saturation coefficient lsc acts on a different concentration scale.
default_locator: angiogenesis_process.py, _run_simulation() specs: decay_global = veder; decay_types["EC"] = 0.0 (no decay inside cells)

description: Rate at which VEGF diffuses through the medium. Controls how quickly VEGF spreads from secreting cells.
admissible_note: The explicit finite-difference step is stable only for D·Δt/Δx² ≤ 0.25 in 2D; DiffusionSolverFE subdivides the MCS to stay under that limit, so larger D costs run time rather than failing outright. 10 site²/MCS is the modeler's cap (40 sub-steps per MCS). D < 0 is meaningless.
supported_evidence: literature: Merks RMH et al. (2006), Merks RMH et al. (2008); Merks et al. 2006, Results ("diffuses slowly at about 1e-13 m² s⁻¹") and Discussion (VEGF165 ≈ 1e-11 m² s⁻¹), p. 50
supported_note: 0.1–2 site²/MCS brackets the Merks value (0.75 site²/MCS at 2 µm, 30 s). Free VEGF-A165 (≈1e-11 m²/s ≈ 75 site²/MCS) lies far above the band and, per Merks 2006, does not produce stable networks in this mechanism — the band therefore encodes the paper's conclusion that the morphogen must be ECM-bound and slow.
recommended_note: Presets 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0. The gradient length L = √(D/ε) is what matters: with ε = 0.3 the band gives L ≈ 1.3–2.2 sites, much shorter than Merks' 5 sites.

description: Rate at which Endothelial Cells secrete VEGF into the surrounding medium.
admissible_note: α ≥ 0 required (negative secretion is uptake, which this field does not model). 2 per MCS is the modeler's cap; the field itself has no upper stability limit on secretion.
supported_evidence: expert_judgement: Merks RMH et al. (2008), Merks RMH et al. (2006); Merks et al. 2008, Methods (Cellular Potts model; chemotaxis; chemoattractant dynamics)
supported_note: 0.1–0.5 per MCS is the model author's band around the default; the literature values (0.0054–0.03 per MCS on the Merks scale) lie below it. Only the ratio to veder is constrained by the papers (α = ε), not the absolute rate.
recommended_note: Presets 0.1 / 0.3 / 0.5. Change together with veder to keep α/ε = 1.

description: How often to save simulation data to Zarr store
admissible_note: At least 1 (every MCS); the upper bound 1,000 equals the longest preset run, above which nothing would ever be written.
supported_note: 5–100 MCS: on the Merks scale 2.5–50 min between frames, fine enough to resolve cell movement at 5 µm/h (one site per 24 min). Execution control.
recommended_note: Presets 5 / 10 / 20 / 50. 10–50 balances I/O cost against time resolution.

description: Total number of Monte Carlo Steps (MCS) to simulate.
supported_evidence: expert_judgement: Merks RMH et al. (2006), Merks RMH et al. (2008); Merks et al. 2006, Fig 5 (0–50 h); Merks et al. 2008, Methods (30 s per MCS), p. 48
supported_note: 10–1,000 MCS. On the Merks scale (30 s per MCS) the default 100 MCS is 50 min and 1,000 MCS is 8.3 h; the in-vitro network coarsening that Merks 2006 Fig 5 reproduces unfolds over 10–50 h (1,200–6,000 MCS). Runs inside this band therefore show network formation but little of the remodelling the papers validate against.
recommended_note: Presets quick 50 / standard 100 / extended 500 / long 1,000 MCS. A practical compute window on a 200×200 lattice, not a biological one.

description: Unique identifier for this simulation run. Used for data storage organization in Zarr hierarchy.
Seed for the Monte Carlo random number generator. Leave at -1 to draw a seed automatically; the drawn value is recorded with the run either way.
admissible_note: -1 asks the wrapper to draw a seed; otherwise any non-negative 32-bit integer accepted by the CompuCell3D random-number generator. Execution control, no biology.
